generated_from.description: Started by todo_sync.py init; items added by todo_sync.py add from open GitHub issues.

ranking_method.score: value / sqrt(cost), multiplied by (1 + unblock_bonus) when the item unblocks at least one item
tie_breakers: primary source type, where the primary source is sources[0]: gh_issue, then impl_stub, then research_folder
primary source ref: issue number ascending for gh_issue, otherwise the ref path in code-point order
primary source item text in code-point order (absent item sorts first)

impact_definitions.silent_wrong_output: A shipped path completes without error or warning and publishes a value or feature that is wrong under an established rule.
impact_definitions.data_correctness: Output or reference data can be wrong or ungoverned, but the correct value still needs a rule or decision to define it, a guard is missing, or the wrong value already surfaces with a warning or error.
impact_definitions.runtime_failure: A path raises or aborts on an input it accepts.
impact_definitions.dev_velocity: Tests, CI or developer tooling are slower, noisier or less trustworthy than they need to be; no output changes.
impact_definitions.maintainability: Structure, duplication, dead code, missing tests or latent defects that no current production path reaches; no output changes.
impact_definitions.docs_tooling: Documentation, research records, configuration or agent tooling outside the shipped paths.

severity_scale.1: Cosmetic or hygiene: renames, dead code, stale docs, a test gap for working or accepted behavior.
severity_scale.2: Debt with a concrete cost, a latent defect that no current path reaches, a missing guard, or a defect that needs a rare or optional input.
severity_scale.3: A wrong or failing result on a supported but uncommon input, or a defect a warning already surfaces.
severity_scale.4: Wrong published output on a common input of a production path, or a failure that blocks a supported workflow.
severity_scale.5: Crashes or corrupts a production path on its normal inputs.

ranking_method.notes: Each item's severity, impact, LoE and blast radius come from its source's triage. Ranking compares scores rounded to 4 decimals; the tie breakers apply in order, so ids and ranks are reproducible from the item fields alone.

items.title: plan.py freeze cannot pass a sweep whose hits include a file deleted after the plan base
items.summary: Per the session: freezing plan 1012 (docs/plans/1012_canned_blocks_survive_build_ActionPlan.json, branch 1150-canned-messages, base 5a8ef39) failed. Sweep S1 (get_canned_message) hit four docs/PR_REVIEWS/*.json files that existed at the base and were deleted from the tree by commit 21df329. `plan.py check` (tree) reports them as 'classified but has no hit' when they are dropped from the classification, and `plan.py freeze` (which also checks sweeps at the base) reports 'at base 5a8ef39: ... has hits but no classification' when they are kept. No classification set satisfies both. The comparison is in sweep_problems (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/plan_checks.py:288), which compares hits to classifications exactly on each side; sweep_hits (plan_checks.py:242) skips only the plans folder and the plan's source_document. Workaround used: S1 pattern narrowed to `^[^"]*get_canned_message` so JSON-string lines drop out; plan 1012 then froze at b4e8d6b. Decision 2026-11-12: option (a). The defect runs both ways: a matching file added on the branch after the plan base also fails one side whichever way it is classified, because freeze runs claim_problems on the tree (plugins/harness/scripts/plan.py:337-341) and base_claim_problems at the base (plan.py:433-444), both from freeze_problems (plan.py:484), and sweep_problems (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/plan_checks.py:286-307) compares hits and classifications exactly on each side, skipping only the plan source document (the e703a52 / #249 precedent). Status checked 2026-11-12: still present in HEAD; no test covers it (tests/lib/test_plan_checks.py has no deleted or absent case).
items.proposed_change: Decision (a): in sweep_problems, suppress the 'is classified but has no hit' line for a classified path that does not exist on the side being checked (git cat-file -e <rev>:<path> at a rev, Path.exists() on the tree); no schema change, no marker label. Add a test that freezes a plan whose sweep hits one file deleted after the base and one added after it. Optional later convenience, not part of the fix: skip history folders from sweep hits via history_paths(cfg) (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/retire.py:222-232).

loe.reasoning: Change is confined to two functions in plan_checks.py plus one test; the option choice is the open cost.

items.title: todo_sync: serialize catalog writes so parallel TODO agents cannot race on RepoToDo.json

items.proposed_change: Decide between (A) a lock file (O_EXCL create with a stale-lock timeout) around every load-modify-write in todo_sync.py, letting agents run add in parallel; and (B) the issue's scratch flow: a new config key (four places: defaults.json, harness.schema.json, config.py, README), agents write one add spec item to scratch, and the main session merges them into one `todo_sync.py add --spec` run. items.title: Driver-created local tags for every necessary, plan-referenced and base-to-freeze commit
items.decision_question: Choose the tag naming scheme (plan/<id>/base, plan/<id>/freeze[-N], strap/<skill>/r<N>/base, strap/<skill>/r<N>/freeze, or the off-branch names already in use), and decide whether a history rewrite moves the tags and re-points spec.base and plan base_commit (requiring a strap.py rebase-base subcommand) or leaves the old commits tagged only.
items.summary: Per the session: the developer wants every necessary commit, every plan-referenced commit and every base-to-freeze range tagged as standing practice, with tags created by the drivers rather than printed as suggestions or checked only. Plan base_commit (plans 1013 and 1014 use 5a8ef39) is necessary: check reads anchors and sweeps at it once an item is done (plugins/harness/scripts/plan.py:265-271). Plan frozen.commit is display only (read at plugins/harness/scripts/plan_render.py:46 and plan_render_html.py:81). Strap spec base (write-plan 9368d9e) is necessary: the baseline arm runs git show <base>:<SKILL.md> (plugins/harness/scripts/strap.py:640), runs start from it (strap.py:391) and reopen refuses a base that does not descend from it (strap.py:911-912). Strap rounds[].base is history only. The strap frozen stamp stores no commit, so a freeze tag would sit at HEAD, one commit before the commit holding the stamp. Receipt evidence holds commit SHA text or staged tree SHA text; a tree SHA cannot be pinned by a tag. Scope: plan.py new tags the plan base, freeze and --refreeze tag the freeze; strap.py new and reopen tag the round base, freeze tags the round freeze; each check warns when a necessary SHA is untagged or unreachable. Tags stay local and the developer pushes them. Building this on a follow-up branch after 2150-plan-refreeze merges, since plan.py and strap.py are parts of the write-plan and strap-skills strap specs and an earlier build would re-stale them. Decided: the drivers create annotated tags (git tag -a, with a message naming the plan or strap round and the SHA role), not lightweight ones, because git push --follow-tags and the push.followTags setting carry only annotated tags that point at commits the push includes; lightweight tags are ignored, and a tag on a commit outside the pushed branch never follows and still needs git push origin <tag>. items.title: session-bookmark: a branch-scoped note goes stale silently after the branch changes
items.decision_question: Which remedy, or which mix: (a) the mod marks or asks about a note that names a branch other than the current one, (b) add-bookmark stores a structured branch scope or a standing flag instead of free-text scoping, or (c) a harness rule that the session says out loud when it judges a stored note not to apply? And should a standing per-turn rule carry over to the next branch by default?
items.summary: Per the session: note 1 read 'For each turn on branch 1153-strap-writing-docstrings: determine the best commit grouping and dispatch those instructions to harness:branch-commit-msg HEAD -- <instructions>'; on 1155-local-review-strapping the session read the branch name as a scope limit, skipped the per-turn dispatch for many turns without saying so, and the developer ran /harness:branch-commit-msg HEAD by hand. Note 2 (next branch after 1154 develops #252 / todo-kex8) was also stale. Checked: a note carries no scope but its text: add_note.py:91-96 stores only added and text; notes.ts:59-64 parseNotes returns the text alone and drops added; bookmark.ts:86-91 prints the notes as a numbered list with no date or branch, while bookmark.ts:100 prints the current branch apart from them, so nothing compares the two. add-bookmark SKILL.md:53-56 tells the writer to spell out the branch in the text, which is how branch scoping ends up as free prose. RESUME_HINT (bookmark.ts:42-45) says nothing about notes, and plugins/harness/rules/HARNESS_RULES.md has no rule on stored notes (no match for bookmark). No stale-note check exists today; whether the session would follow a marked note is unverified. Related: #272 (open, untracked) asks for removing or editing one note, which would let a stale note be dropped without clear; todo-ys3k (#204) is the only catalog item on bookmark.ts.
items.proposed_change: Per the decision. (a) Mod only: in formatBookmark, mark a note whose text names a branch other than b.branch (match against branch-like tokens, or the local branch list) with a visible stale marker and ask the session to confirm it with the developer before applying or dropping it; heuristic, no schema change. (b) Structured scope: add_note.py records the current branch (or takes --branch / --standing) in each entry; parseNotes keeps the field; noteLines prints it and flags a mismatch with b.branch; a standing note prints as applying on every branch. Needs the field mirrored in notes.ts and pinned in test_session_bookmark_notes_contract.py, and a NOTES_VERSION decision (an optional field avoids the bump). (c) Rule: HARNESS_RULES.md (and the bookmark's notes header) says a session that judges a stored note not to apply states that and asks, never drops it silently. (b) plus a one-line (c) header is the most robust; (a) is the cheapest. Pair with #272 so a stale note can be removed singly.

items.title: strap: pin judgment greens to the parts a scenario runner reads, so library and driver edits stop staling frozen specs
items.decision_question: Which hash scope should strap use: (A) one runner-read hash, chosen by a per-part flag that defaults by kind; (B) a rule based on kind alone, after retagging parts; (C) two hashes, where a runner hash pins greens and an all-parts hash raises a drift line that a test-only refreeze clears; or (D) keep the hash and only fix the stale wording? And does a driver whose printed lines the SKILL.md quotes count as runner-read?
items.summary: Developer note: fix the strap side first, because it causes the most refreezes. Judgment greens would hash only the parts a runner sees (SKILL.md, README, agent files), and CI's mechanical tests would cover library and driver parts. Before the change, a plan.py fix makes write-plan stale, and clearing it takes 2 runner greens and a refreeze. After it, the same fix needs nothing beyond CI. This changes what the content hash means, so it is a design item, not a ready fix. Origin, per the session: the session reviewed whether the write-plan receipts rewrite (issue 258, spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-plan-receipts-design.md, branch 2150-plan-refreeze, not on main) meets its goal that a frozen plan is never written during execution. Plan freezes mostly hold: plan 1014 was frozen once at 88659f1, and mid-build changes went to EX1/EX2 in docs/plans/1014/DesignEvolution.json. Most refreeze churn on this lineage comes from the strap skill-spec freeze, which the rewrite does not touch. Cause: plugins/harness/scripts/strap.py:219-221 `skill_hash` hashes every listed part through plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/strap_runs.py:24-34 `content_hash`, so one changed byte in any part (library module, driver or contract test) moves the hash. strap.py:224-232 `stale_line` then prints `stale: frozen at <old>, parts now hash <new>; prove greens then freeze --refreeze`. Checked on 2026-11-10 by running this checkout's `strap.py check` on each spec: 5 of the 8 specs under docs/plans/strap/ are stale: add-todo (5422c856e8fa -> 1cf10e2e8d8e), c-msg (67c817fe42db -> 7072c6396257), merge-commit-msg (a474c565ad45 -> ec925d971a76), review-local (8538f7298472 -> 579fe2d58a9c) and todo-edit (0fd83b8e96f8 -> 1bab6480cca1). write-plan and writing-docstrings are current. strap-skills has no frozen stamp, so check prints no stale line for it. Parts and live judgment behaviors per spec (counted from each SkillSpec.json): add-todo 6/2, c-msg 7/0, merge-commit-msg 4/0, review-local 8/3, strap-skills 12/0, todo-edit 3/0, write-plan 14/2, writing-docstrings 8/3. c-msg, merge-commit-msg and todo-edit have no judgment behavior, so the `prove greens` wording misleads for them: their refreeze only reruns planned tests (strap.py:856-868 `_planned_tests_pass` / `_mechanical_gate`). write-plan lists 14 parts: SKILL.md, README.md, two contract tests, plus ten code parts: plan.py, plan_models.py, plan_enums.py, plan_doc.py, plan_record.py, plan_render.py, plan_receipts.py, receipt_models.py, plan_render_html.py and evolution_api.py. The receipts rewrite added the last four. Concrete cost: PR 262 review M1 (docs/PR_REVIEWS/0262_Featurestrap_reopen_command.json:171, resolved at d34fc56) changed one sentence of plugins/harness/skills/write-plan/README.md. That moved the write-plan hash from d3fd6c04afdb to 63707d01db1e and forced green R-6 (B9, SC-1; docs/plans/strap/write-plan/SkillSpec.json:802-806) before the round-3 freeze at 63707d01db1e (SkillSpec.json:877). The note counts README as runner-read, so that run would still be required under the proposal; the saving applies to library and driver edits. Whether a runner ever opens README is unverified: a run brief carries the SKILL.md (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/strap_models.py:250-253 `skill_in_brief`). Hash consumers in strap.py: `_needs` :472-477 (one green per scenario and hash), `cmd_run` :608-613 (pins a new run to the current hash), `_refuse_twin` :711-715, `cmd_retest` :800-802 (refuses while the hash equals the failed green's), `_passed_greens` :829-831 and `_judgment_gate` :834-853 (freeze needs a passing green on the current hash), `cmd_freeze` :892-898 (stamps `Frozen.skill_hash`), `stale_line` (printed by `new` on resume at :257 and by `check` at :380), and `cmd_reopen` :933-934 (moves the stamp into `rounds`). `Frozen.authored` (strap_models.py:384-394, digest at :532-541) seals the authored fields. Those fields include the parts list but not part contents, so a change of hash scope leaves the seal alone unless `Part` gains a field. Part kinds cannot pick the runner-read set as they stand. write-plan tags both plan_enums.py and README.md as `reference`, and merge-commit-msg tags commands/merge_commit_msg.py as `reference` (strap_models.py:73-82 `PartKind`). No test gates on staleness: the `stale` hit in tests/contract/test_root_separation.py:180-188 concerns an ArcGIS toolbox, not strap. The rule text lives in plugins/harness/skills/strap-skills/SKILL.md:62-64 (green pinned to the content hash of every part file) and :224-236 (refreeze after a part change). Related catalog items on strap.py: todo-v55s (#178, scenario tree branch), todo-7sfy (comparison arm) and todo-66qe (#254, recorder paths). Per the session: re-proving a rule that is already written needs a strip-and-restore base (write-plan round 3, 9368d9e then a5852a7).
items.proposed_change: Start with a short design pass, then implement the option the developer picks. Before/after trace of each hash consumer under the runner-read scope: (1) Green pinning (`_needs`, `cmd_run`, `_refuse_twin`). Before: any part edit makes every judgment behavior need a new green. After: only an edit to a runner-read part does. (2) `cmd_retest`. Before: a library or driver fix changes the hash, so a failed green can be retested. After: the hash stays the same, so `retest` would refuse `skill unchanged` even after the real fix. Retest must compare the all-parts hash, or the design must accept the refusal. (3) Freeze gate (`_judgment_gate`, `_mechanical_gate`). Greens are checked on the runner hash, and planned tests still run at freeze. (4) `stale_line` in `check` and `new`. It fires only on runner-part edits. Drift in mechanical parts goes silent (A) or gets its own `drift:` line (C). Also fix the wording for specs with no judgment behavior, which have no greens to prove. (5) `Frozen` stamp and `rounds`. Existing stamps hold the all-parts hash, so a switch in meaning makes every frozen spec stale at once. Add a scope field to `Frozen` and `Run`. Compare old stamps under the old rule until their next refreeze. Have `_dumped` (strap_models.py:515-529) drop the field at its default so the authored digests of existing specs stay byte for byte. Update plugins/harness/schemas/SkillSpec.schema.json (:223, :488). (6) `Frozen.authored` seal. It is unchanged unless `Part` gains a flag; a flag needs the same default-drop in `_dumped`. Options: (A) Add a per-part `runner_reads` flag. It defaults by kind: skill_md and agent true; models, api, driver and contract_test false; reference set explicitly. Greens pin to the hash of the flagged parts. This matches the note's After: a plan.py fix needs only CI. (B) Use kind alone, after adding kinds such as `library` and `doc` and retagging every spec. This needs no new field, but a mis-tag silently drops a part from the hash. (C) Keep two hashes. The runner hash pins greens. The all-parts hash raises a `drift:` line, and a refreeze clears it by rerunning planned tests with no greens. This keeps a record, but every library fix still costs a refreeze. (D) Keep today's hash and fix only the stale wording. Recommendation: A, with a scope version on the stamp and retest comparing the all-parts hash. Accepted risk: a driver change that alters lines the SKILL.md tells the session to read would get past the greens. Close that gap with contract tests that pin those lines, which CI runs, or by flagging that driver `runner_reads`. Then update strap-skills SKILL.md (Rules :62-64 and step 12 :224-236). Add tests to tests/lib/test_strap_runs.py, tests/scripts/test_strap_gate.py and tests/scripts/test_strap_reopen.py covering: a library-only edit leaves the spec current, a runner-part edit makes it stale, an old stamp compares under the old scope, and retest unblocks after a driver fix.

blast_radius.reasoning: Changes what the content hash means for every strap consumer in strap.py, and adds a scope field to the Frozen and Run models and the schema. All 7 frozen specs under docs/plans/strap/ need a migration rule so they do not go stale at once.

loe.reasoning: A design pass, then a hash-scope change across strap.py, strap_runs and strap_models, a schema field with a byte-stable default, a migration rule for existing stamps, a retest fix, a SKILL.md rewrite of the pinning rule and step 12, and tests in three files.

items.decision_question: Which `local_llm.*` key names (enabled, base_url, model, num_ctx, timeout_seconds) ship, and is the harness:c-msg draft step the trial consumer?
items.summary: No driver, config key or consumer exists: a Grep for `ollama` and `local_llm` over the repo finds nothing. The issue specifies a standard-library (`urllib`) driver calling `POST /api/chat` with `stream:false` and `think:false`, `options.num_ctx` sized from the input, and a distinct exit code on connection refused, timeout or empty content so the calling skill falls back to the hosted model. Per CLAUDE.md, the endpoint, model and limits are a new config key touching plugins/harness/config/defaults.json, config/harness.schema.json, lib/harness_lib/config.py and the README key table. items.proposed_change: Add the `local_llm` config block (default disabled) in the four places, a driver script under plugins/harness/scripts/ that posts to the configured base URL and returns text or a fallback exit code, tests against a stub HTTP server through the `make_project` fixture (success, `think:false` in the body, `num_ctx` sized from input, timeout and empty content fallback), and wire the c-msg draft step behind `local_llm.enabled` with a format check on real diffs before any default-on.
